identification.summary: Russia-based espionage actor focused on credential theft through tailored spear-phishing against high-profile people in government, defense, think tanks, academia, NGOs and journalism, mostly in NATO countries [S1][S2][S3]. Microsoft says it supports espionage and cyber-influence objectives, including occasional hack-and-leak operations [S1][S2]. The UK NCSC and Five Eyes partners assess it is almost certainly subordinate to FSB Centre 18 [S3][S4]. Since 2023-2025 it has added selective malware (SPICA, LOSTKEYS, and the NOROBOT/MAYBEROBOT chain) to its phishing work [S8][S9][S11].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft has tracked the actor since 2017 [S2]. NCSC reports spear-phishing of UK parliamentarians since at least 2015 and an Institute for Statecraft compromise in 2018 [S4]. Press coverage of Google TAG reporting says targeting dates to at least 2015 [S9].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Star Blizzard (formerly SEABORGIUM; renamed April 2023). Microsoft notes overlaps with Callisto Group (F-Secure), TA446 (Proofpoint) and COLDRIVER (Google) [S2]. Google lists COLDRIVER as also known as UNC4057, Star Blizzard and Callisto [S8]. The joint advisory lists SEABORGIUM, Callisto Group, TA446, COLDRIVER, TAG-53 and BlueCharlie [S3]. Microsoft did not confirm a link to Gamaredon/ACTINIUM that Ukraine's SSU proposed [S2]. Citizen Lab's COLDWASTREL is a separate cluster [S10].

attribution.sponsor: Russian Federation. The UK NCSC and partners in the US, Australia, Canada and New Zealand assess that Star Blizzard is almost certainly subordinate to FSB Centre 18 [S3][S4]. DOJ describes Centre 18 as the FSB unit involved [S5][S6].
attribution.confidence: Government: NCSC uses 'almost certainly' for Centre 18 subordination (December 2023) [S3][S4]. Microsoft attributes the actor to Russia and says its objectives align with Russian state interests, with no formal confidence rating [S2]. Google calls COLDRIVER 'Russian government-backed' without naming an agency [S8].
attribution.basis: Five Eyes joint advisory and UK attribution statement [S3][S4]. A US indictment (unsealed December 2023) charges Ruslan Peretyatko, described as an FSB Centre 18 officer, and Andrey Korinets, and the US and UK imposed sanctions [S5]. Microsoft and Google telemetry and infrastructure analysis [S1][S2][S8]. Microsoft and DOJ domain seizures in October 2024 [S6].

objectives: Intelligence collection supporting Russia's strategic interests [S8]. Microsoft also cites cyber-influence objectives [S1][S2]. Stolen material has been selectively leaked to advance Russian goals, including undermining trust in UK politics [S4][S12]. The actor has also targeted exiled Russian opposition figures and civil society [S10].

sectors: Defense, intelligence consultancies and defense-industrial organizations [S2][S3]
regions: United States and United Kingdom (most affected) [S2][S3]
targeting.notes: The actor mainly targets personal webmail accounts rather than corporate ones [S3]. Microsoft says about 30% of its related nation-state notifications went to consumer accounts [S2]. Microsoft observed targeting of more than 30 civil-society organizations between January 2023 and August 2024 [S6].

capabilities.summary: Core trade: research on targets, fake profiles and impersonation of trusted contacts, followed by rapport-building emails sent from webmail accounts (Outlook, Gmail, Yahoo, Proton) [S2][S3]. It harvests credentials with Evilginx adversary-in-the-middle phishing, which captures MFA tokens [S1]. Lures include PDFs (some password-protected) hosted on Proton Drive, URL shorteners, open redirects, Microsoft Safe Links wrapping, and the HubSpot and MailerLite email marketing platforms (2023) [S1]. It evades detection with a DNS/reverse-proxy service, anti-automation scripts, hCaptcha, randomized domains and multiple registrars [S1]. After compromise it exfiltrates mailboxes and sets forwarding rules to dead-drop accounts [S2]. In 2024 it took over WhatsApp accounts by luring targets to scan a QR code that linked their account to an actor-controlled device [S7]. Selective malware includes: the Rust backdoor SPICA, delivered as a fake decryption tool and used since about November 2022 [S9]; LOSTKEYS, a VBS file stealer delivered by a ClickFix fake CAPTCHA (January-April 2025) [S8]; and, after LOSTKEYS was exposed, the COLDCOPY lure, NOROBOT DLL and YESROBOT/MAYBEROBOT backdoors (2025) [S11].

campaigns.name: Institute for Statecraft compromise
campaigns.summary: NCSC says the UK think tank was compromised in 2018 and documents were later leaked; its founder's account was compromised from December 2021.

campaigns.name: UK-US trade documents leak
campaigns.summary: NCSC cites the leak of UK-US trade documents ahead of the 2019 UK general election.

campaigns.name: Brexit proponents email leak
campaigns.summary: Emails allegedly stolen from Brexit proponents' ProtonMail accounts were leaked. Microsoft independently linked the campaign to SEABORGIUM through technical indicators.

campaigns.name: Microsoft SEABORGIUM disruption
campaigns.summary: Microsoft disabled actor accounts and published IOCs, citing more than 30 organizations targeted since the start of 2022.

campaigns.name: SPICA backdoor deployment
campaigns.summary: Google TAG saw the SPICA backdoor delivered by fake PDF decryption tools from early September 2023 and believes it has been used since November 2022.

campaigns.name: Five Eyes advisory, indictment and sanctions
campaigns.summary: Joint advisory attributes Star Blizzard to FSB Centre 18; the US charges Peretyatko and Korinets; the US and UK impose sanctions.

campaigns.name: 'River of Phish' campaign against civil society
campaigns.summary: Citizen Lab and Access Now report COLDRIVER phishing of exiled Russians, former US officials and NGOs, including impersonation of people known to targets.

campaigns.name: Microsoft/DOJ domain takedown
campaigns.summary: A Microsoft civil order covered 66 domains and DOJ seized 41 more used by Star Blizzard.

campaigns.name: WhatsApp account-takeover phishing
campaigns.summary: Lures impersonating a US government official used QR codes to link targets' WhatsApp accounts to actor devices. Microsoft disclosed the campaign in January 2025.

campaigns.name: LOSTKEYS ClickFix malware
campaigns.summary: GTIG observed LOSTKEYS delivered by a fake CAPTCHA in January, March and April 2025.

campaigns.name: ROBOT malware chain
campaigns.summary: After LOSTKEYS was exposed, GTIG reports COLDRIVER moved to the COLDCOPY, NOROBOT and YESROBOT/MAYBEROBOT chain, with MAYBEROBOT appearing by June 2025.

diamond.adversary: FSB Centre 18-linked operators (NCSC: almost certainly) [S3][S4]. US charges name Peretyatko (FSB officer) and Korinets (alleged co-conspirator) [S5].
diamond.capability: Evilginx AiTM credential theft; PDF and link lures; WhatsApp device linking; SPICA, LOSTKEYS and NOROBOT/MAYBEROBOT malware [S1][S7][S8][S9][S11].
diamond.infrastructure: Batch-registered domains (Namecheap, Hostinger and others) with Let's Encrypt certificates; paired VPS redirector and Evilginx servers; a DNS/reverse-proxy service; email marketing platforms; Proton Drive file hosting; webmail sender accounts [S1][S3].
diamond.victim: Government, defense, think tank, academic, NGO and journalist individuals in the US, the UK and NATO, often through personal email [S2][S3][S8].
diamond.socioPolitical: Collection on Russia, Ukraine and NATO policy; hack-and-leak operations to undermine trust in UK politics; pressure on Russian dissidents abroad [S4][S10][S12].
diamond.technology: Consumer webmail and cloud email, MFA that can be phished, WhatsApp linked-device features, and Windows scripting (PowerShell, rundll32) [S1][S7][S8][S11].

gaps: Primary government documents were not opened: the joint advisory PDF, the NCSC pages, the DOJ press release and the indictment were unreachable or blocked. Their content is taken from search summaries and press coverage [S3][S4][S5][S6].
The GTIG October 2025 ROBOT-chain report and Zscaler's BAITSWITCH/SIMPLEFIX report (a mapping that comes from press coverage) were not opened directly [S11].
Microsoft's January 2025 WhatsApp blog was seen only through secondary coverage and an update note on the 2023 blog [S1][S7].

Original Google TAG SPICA blog, Citizen Lab 'River of Phish' report, F-Secure Callisto report and Recorded Future TAG-53/BlueCharlie reports were not opened; vendor cluster overlaps (TAG-53, BlueCharlie, IRON FRONTIER, GOSSAMER BEAR) are not independently verified here.
Relationship to Citizen Lab's COLDWASTREL cluster and the SSU-proposed Gamaredon link are unresolved [S2][S10].
Google could not confirm whether December 2023 Maltego-themed LOSTKEYS samples are COLDRIVER's [S8].
Activity after October 2025 was not researched.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1: Key terrain is the personal and cloud email accounts, messaging apps (WhatsApp) and home devices of senior leaders, policy advisers, defense-industrial staff and Ukraine-support logistics personnel. Much of this sits outside DoD network boundaries [S1][S3][S7]. STEP 2: The actor's reliance on credible impersonation and phishable MFA makes identity and personal accounts the operating environment. Rapid infrastructure turnover after exposure shortens the useful life of indicators [S1][S6]. STEP 3: The doctrinal template is reconnaissance and a fake persona, a benign rapport email, a PDF or link lure, Evilginx or QR-code device linking, then mailbox exfiltration and forwarding rules. A selective malware branch delivers ClickFix PowerShell leading to LOSTKEYS or the NOROBOT/MAYBEROBOT chain [S1][S2][S7][S8][S11]. STEP 4: MLCOA is continued credential phishing of personal accounts of US, UK and NATO defense and policy figures for intelligence on Ukraine support. MDCOA is a timed hack-and-leak of stolen planning or political correspondence during a crisis or election to undermine allied cohesion [S4][S12]. Candidate indicators: unsolicited emails from known contacts on new webmail addresses; password-protected PDFs on Proton Drive; Safe Links-wrapped shortened URLs; new inbox forwarding rules; unexpected WhatsApp linked devices; rundll32 or PowerShell launched from the Run dialog after a CAPTCHA page [S1][S2][S7][S8][S11].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: the victims are mostly personal and NGO accounts, so DoD sensors will miss much of this activity. JCC2 pictures should include partner reporting from NCSC, Microsoft and Google notifications [S2][S3][S8]. (2) Authorities: personal accounts and commercial messaging platforms fall outside DoDIN defensive authorities. Response depends on FBI, DOJ and industry actions such as the October 2024 domain seizures [S5][S6]. (3) Mission assurance: phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2) and personal-account hygiene for key leaders and Ukraine-support logistics staff reduce exposure to AiTM credential theft [S1]. (4) Coordination: share indicators with Five Eyes partners and the DIB, and expect the actor to rebuild infrastructure quickly after exposure [S3][S6].
